ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The shaded part in the figure is a horizontal strip-shaped figure; the right end is an arc-shaped semicircle, and a V-shaped triangular notch is cut out from the left end. The figure labels the straight part of the strip as having length 19 and height 6; the diameter of the right-end arc is the same as the height of the strip, 6, so the radius is 3. The enlarged diagram below shows that the left V-shaped notch is formed by two sides labeled 6, with an included angle of 60°, so this notch can be regarded as an equilateral triangle with side length 6. Reasoning and calculation: Decompose the shaded area into a 19×6 rectangle, plus a semicircle on the right end with radius 3, and subtract the equilateral triangular notch on the left with side length 6. The area of the rectangle is 19×6=114. The area of the semicircle is (1/2)π×3²=4.5π≈14.13. The area of the equilateral triangle is (√3/4)×6²=9√3≈15.59. So the total area is about 114+14.13−15.59=112.54, rounded to 112.5.

raw_record.question_text: Find the area of the figure.

method.method_draft: Decompose the shaded figure into a 19 by 6 rectangle, plus a right semicircle, minus the left V-shaped triangular notch. From the image, read the strip height as 6, the straight rectangular length as 19, and the rounded right end as a semicircle with diameter 6, so radius 3. The inset detail shows the notch is made from two length-6 sides meeting at a 60° angle, so it is an equilateral triangle of side 6; equivalently its base is 6 and height is 3√3. Compute area = 19·6 + (1/2)π·3² − (√3/4)·6². Using π≈3.14 and √3≈1.732 gives 114 + 14.13 − 15.59 ≈ 112.5.
